adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration is dereferenced without optional chaining, so any booking with no destinationCalendar throws TypeError and the whole create/reschedule flow crashes

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — updateEvent fallback `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always resolves to undefined and the destinationCalendar fallback is dead — updates go to an undefined calendarId

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, updateEvent computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. The `find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g. undefined/null), but then it searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e. `=== undefined/null`), which will almost always return no match, making `selectedCalendar` undefined. Unlike createEvent (which falls back to "primary"), updateEvent then passes this undefined calendarId into `calendar.events.update`, so the intended destinationCalendar fallback is effectively dead and can lead to updates targeting an invalid/undefined calendarId. The same flawed pattern is also introduced in deleteEvent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — deleteEvent has the same dead-fallback find, so cancels with no stored externalCalendarId silently fail and leave orphaned Google events on hosts' calendars

adjudication.rationale:
In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent, the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is not provided is:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will not match normal calendars and therefore yields `undefined`. That makes the computed `calendarId` effectively unusable for deleting events from a non-primary calendar (and likely results in deleting against the wrong calendar or failing to delete), which can leave orphaned events. This is a concrete logic bug introduced by the diff’s array refactor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:336 — createAllCalendarEvents does not dedupe destinations, so a shared/team destination calendar equal to a member's yields two identical events in the same calendar

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` to iterate over `event.destinationCalendar` entries and create events per entry (or per matching credential when `credentialId` is missing), but nothing in the diff demonstrates that `destinationCalendar` will contain duplicate entries representing the same underlying calendar (e.g., a team destination and a member destination that resolve to the same credential/externalId). The code indeed does not dedupe, but the proposed finding depends on how `destinationCalendar` is constructed elsewhere (not shown here), so the “shared/team destination calendar equals a member’s yields two identical events in the same calendar” scenario is not directly verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:336 — No rollback or partial-failure handling: if a later host's calendar write fails the earlier hosts' events remain, and the booking is still reported successful

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts (createAllCalendarEvents), the diff changes destinationCalendar to an array and then iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` creating calendar events one-by-one. If a later `createEvent(...)` call fails (e.g., returns an EventResult with `success: false`), there is no compensation/rollback logic to delete events already created for earlier destinations, nor any early abort. This makes partial success possible and can leave earlier hosts’ calendar events persisted while others fail. The part about the booking still being reported successful depends on upstream logic not shown here, but the lack of rollback/partial-failure handling in this function is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — Fallback lookup find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always resolves undefined and the destination-calendar contract is effectively lost on update/delete (same at line 317)

adjudication.rationale:
In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback branch is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

(and similarly for `calendarId` in deleteEvent).

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only time the fallback runs), the `find` predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to that same falsy `externalCalendarId` (typically `undefined`/`null`), so it will almost always return `undefined`. This means the intended destination-calendar selection is effectively lost in the fallback path (it no longer falls back to a destination calendar’s externalId, unlike the pre-diff logic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:542 — credential may still be undefined after the DB lookup fails, yet updateEvent is called with it, propagating undefined instead of skipping/erroring

packages/core/EventManager.ts:598 — Error path now returns [] when the throw happens before calendarReference is assigned (and dropped the console.error), so failures are silently reported as success instead of one failed EventResult

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the catch block behavior changed. Previously, regardless of whether `calendarReference` was assigned, it returned `Promise.resolve([{ success: false, ... }])` (with `type: calendarReference?.type || "calendar"`), ensuring at least one failed `EventResult` was reported. After the change, `calendarReference` is an array and the catch returns `calendarReference?.map(...) ?? ([] as Array<EventResult<NewCalendarEventType>>)`.

If an exception is thrown before `calendarReference` is set (or if it remains `undefined`), this now returns `[]`, which can cause upstream code to interpret the operation as “no results” rather than “failure,” i.e., the failure is no longer surfaced via a failed `EventResult`. The removal of `console.error(message)` also reduces observability, but the core correctness regression is the empty-array return on early failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — Per-destination-calendar prisma.credential.findUnique inside the loop creates N+1 DB queries for collective events.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts (createAllCalendarEvents), the new logic iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and, when a matching credential isn’t already in `this.calendarCredentials`, performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } ... })` inside that loop. For events with multiple destination calendars (or many missing from the in-memory list), this results in one DB query per destination, i.e., an N+1 query pattern that is directly observable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:370 — createEvent is awaited sequentially per destination, serializing N external calendar API calls instead of running them in parallel.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts within createAllCalendarEvents, the new logic iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and does `const createdEvent = await createEvent(...)` inside the loop. This makes each destination calendar event creation wait for the previous one to finish, so N destination calendars cause N external API calls to run sequentially. This is verifiable from the diff and can be a performance/latency regression compared to using Promise.all for parallelism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:517 — Credential lookup by findUnique inside the per-reference update loop is an awaited N+1 query and also blocks the otherwise-parallel updateEvent batch.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts, inside the new `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop, when a matching credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the code does `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` for that reference before pushing `updateEvent(...)` into `result`. This introduces a per-reference awaited DB lookup (N+1 pattern) and serializes those lookups, preventing the updates from being queued fully in parallel until after each DB call completes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — Fallback `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can only match when externalCalendarId is truthy, so the fallback always yields undefined calendarId and the update silently targets nothing

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — Same self-defeating fallback in deleteEvent: when externalCalendarId is falsy the find never matches, so stale calendar events are never deleted

adjudication.rationale:
In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent, the new fallback logic is:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (the condition for taking the fallback branch), the `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to `undefined`, which will almost never match. So even if `event.destinationCalendar` is populated, this expression returns `undefined`, causing deletion to fall back to the default ("primary") later. That is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff: it will not delete from the intended destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing, leading to events remaining undeleted (or attempting deletion in the wrong calendar).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:597 — The catch block dropped the console.error(message) call, so update failures are now swallowed with no log before returning synthetic failure results

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts the catch block previously did `console.error(message);` before returning a synthetic failure result array. In the diff, that `console.error(message)` line is removed and there is no replacement logging call in the catch. The function still returns failure results, but the error message is no longer logged at this point, reducing observability of update failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:356 — When the credential is missing or its app slug is null the destination is silently skipped: no event created, no error, no result entry, so partial failures are invisible

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new loop over `event.destinationCalendar` only pushes a result when it can resolve a `credential` (either from `this.calendarCredentials` or from DB when `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is truthy). If the credential isn’t found, or it is found in DB but `app.slug` is null/undefined, `credential` remains undefined and the code simply doesn’t call `createEvent` and doesn’t add any failure `EventResult` entry for that destination (it just falls through). This makes partial failures (some destinations skipped) invisible to callers because there is no error and no result entry for the skipped destination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — The recurring-event delete loop is now nested inside the per-reference loop, so each remaining booking is deleted once per calendar reference (duplicate API calls)

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, bookingCalendarReference changed from a single reference (find) to an array (filter), and the code now iterates `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside that per-reference loop, the recurring-event deletion branch builds `promises` over **all** `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(..._calendar)` and then loops `for (const updBooking of updatedBookings)` deleting each remaining booking’s calendar event. Because this recurring-delete logic does not depend on the outer `reference` (it uses all credentials and updatedBookings), it will run once per calendar reference, causing duplicate deleteEvent API calls when there are multiple `_calendar` references.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:154 — When no destination matches the credentialId the event silently falls back to "primary", writing a collective event onto the wrong calendar rather than failing

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now selects the target calendar via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, but then calls `calendar.events.insert` with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. This means if `destinationCalendar` is provided but none of its entries match the passed `credentialId` (e.g., entries lack `credentialId` or there’s a mismatch), the code silently falls back to inserting the event into the authenticated account’s `primary` calendar instead of failing or signaling a mismatch. That behavior is directly present in the diff and can lead to creating the event on an unintended calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:470 — apiDeletes collects raw promises whose rejections are not individually handled, so one failing calendar delete can reject the whole batch or surface as an unhandled rejection

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — updateEvent fallback find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) is unreachable/always undefined; no test would catch this dead branch

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — deleteEvent has the same self-contradictory find fallback with no coverage for the externalCalendarId-absent case

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the new fallback logic in deleteEvent is self-contradictory: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is absent (undefined/null), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will almost never match a real calendar externalId, so `calendarId` becomes undefined instead of falling back to a sensible destination calendar (e.g., the first entry) or reliably to `primary`. This mirrors the same flawed pattern introduced in updateEvent and is a correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:1 — Cancellation loop over multiple booking calendar references (incl. DB credential fallback) is untested; risk of double-delete or missed deletes for collective bookings

The recurring-event deletion logic (building `promises` over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and deleting events for `updatedBookings`) now sits inside that per-reference loop. If there are multiple `_calendar` references (which is exactly why `.filter` was introduced), this recurring deletion block can execute multiple times, attempting to delete the same set of events repeatedly (double-deletes) and pushing duplicate results into `apiDeletes`. That is a concrete behavioral change and a verifiable correctness risk introduced by the diff, independent of whether tests exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — Lark/Office365 services silently pick only the first destination calendar; no test documents this intentional limitation for collective events

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array (`DestinationCalendar[] | null`). In both `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now destructures only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? The “no test documents this limitation” part isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the silent “first element only” behavior (and resulting incorrectness for multi-destination events) is real and introduced/retained by this diff.
